purpose: Root-cause ladder for the 1j/2j MadGraph zero-cross-section blocker encountered during strong-bm1 independent generation.
symptom: MadGraph5_aMC@NLO 3.5.3 'Survey return zero cross section' for p p > go go j (and p p > go go j j) using the mission-mandated generated SLHA (m_gluino=2000 GeV, m_neutralino=850 GeV, decoupled sfermions at 4.5e5 GeV per the public ALessa template). All 99 integration channels report exactly 0.00000E+00, not a small nonzero value. Repeated IEEE_INVALID_FLAG warnings appear only in failing runs.

runs.result: zero cross section, all channels, IEEE_INVALID_FLAG present
zero cross section, all 99 channels literally 0.00000E+00 (checked results.dat directly), IEEE_INVALID_FLAG present. Rules out survey-statistics starvation as the cause.

runs.param_card: diagnostic only (not committed): production SLHA with sfermion masses lowered 4.5e5 -> 3.0e3 GeV, gluino/neutralino unchanged at 2000/850
runs.result: still zero cross section, same 'No points passed cuts!' pattern. Rules out the specific 4.5e5 GeV magnitude as uniquely responsible; a merely 'heavy relative to gluino' squark (3 TeV vs 2000 GeV gluino) already reproduces the failure.

runs.param_card: MG5's own untouched MSSM_SLHA2 default param_card (m_gluino=607.7 GeV, m_squark~550-570 GeV, i.e. squark LIGHTER than gluino)
runs.result: SUCCEEDS: cross section 8.25 +/- 0.11 pb, 0 IEEE_INVALID_FLAG occurrences. Proves the proc/run cards and MG5/environment are functionally correct in general.

runs.param_card: MG5 default param_card with ONLY m_gluino edited to 2000 GeV (m_squark left at default ~550-570 GeV, i.e. squark now LIGHTER than gluino by construction)
runs.result: SUCCEEDS: cross section 0.000567 +/- 0.0000071 pb, 0 IEEE_INVALID_FLAG occurrences. Isolates that m_gluino=2000 GeV alone is NOT the cause.

free_checks.slha_source_mismatch: diff of GCottin's own 0_mg5_cards/GG_qqn1_2800_10_rpvLF_p01ns.slha vs the ALessa validation copy used as source: BYTE IDENTICAL (diff exit 0). Rules out a card-pairing mistake.
free_checks.ieee_correlation: grep IEEE_INVALID_FLAG: 10 occurrences in the failing prod_1000ev run, 0 occurrences in the working default_mssm_slha2 run.

ruled_out: run/proc card mismatch or corruption (byte-identical to upstream)
survey statistics starvation (fails identically at 10 and 1000 events, literal exact zero in every channel)
the specific 4.5e5 GeV magnitude alone (3 TeV squarks reproduce the same failure)
m_gluino=2000 GeV alone (works fine with light ~550 GeV squarks)

cuts being generically too strict (ptj/etaj/ktdurham are unchanged between working and failing configurations; a 9 TeV headroom in sqrt(s_hat) makes a hard-cut rejection of literally 100% of 5,000,000 sampled points implausible)
conclusion.root_cause_candidate: The failure requires BOTH a squark mass scale decoupled well above the gluino mass (>=3 TeV squark vs 2000 GeV gluino) AND a real-emission/merging-relevant final state (1j/2j; the 2-body 0j process is unaffected at the same decoupled-squark SLHA). This points to the MLM-merging/jet-clustering machinery (cluster.f / sudakov.inc / the ktdurham- and xqcut-related kinematic bookkeeping compiled into each process's SubProcesses tree) mis-evaluating a merging-scale-related kinematic quantity (observed as an overflowed 's min' print field and IEEE_INVALID_FLAG) when a super-heavy propagator mass is present, causing every sampled phase-space point to be rejected before the physical cuts are even applied.
conclusion.confidence: Isolated by direct experiment to 'decoupled squark scale x real-emission topology'; the precise Fortran-level mechanism inside cluster.f/setcuts.f was not traced further, per the mission's diagnostic time-box.
conclusion.not_yet_tested: Whether the original author's own bm1 generation used a materially different squark decoupling scale, a different MG5 patch/version, or an explicit MG5 'set' command (e.g. disabling amplitude suppression or the MLM cluster veto) not present in the public proc/run cards inspected here.
conclusion.minimum_next_action: Ask whether the author's private generation setup applied any non-default MG5 'set' commands (e.g. related to amplitude suppression, cluster scale, or cutoff parameters) when generating the 1j/2j strong-bm1 samples with decoupled sfermions -- or consult MadGraph documentation/support on MLM-merging behavior when spectator sfermions are set far above the hard-process scale. This mission's instructions explicitly forbid re-contacting the author during this run, so this is deferred to the user.
